mainTopic: ריש לקיש's view that dawn permits the new grain, רבא on a עומר offered with wrong intent, and why a פסוק is needed to exclude a טרפה from the מזבח.
overview: The amud opens by finishing ריש לקיש's rule that dawn of the sixteenth of ניסן permits the new grain (חדש). The גמרא shows that he never said this outright. It is inferred from his ruling that new-grain offerings brought on the sixteenth, even before the עומר, are כשר. רבא then rules that a מנחת העומר whose handful was taken שלא לשמה is fully כשר, because wrong intent only works with a fit person, a fit item and a fit place. A ברייתא next learns from the extra words 'מן הבקר' that a טרפה may not be offered. It also tests whether a קל וחומר could teach this instead, going back and forth with חלב and דם and with מליקה. The גמרא asks which refutation the ברייתא had in mind. רב suggests the עומר, ריש לקיש the קטורת, מר בריה דרבינא שבת, and רב אדא בר אבא כלאים. Each one is rejected, mostly because those cases are themselves a מצוה and offering a טרפה is not. The rejection of רב אדא בר אבא's כלאים proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's rule: dawn permits the new grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting ריש לקיש's opinion that dawn of the sixteenth of ניסן permits the new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rising light in the east permits the new grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a quote of ריש לקיש's rule, which started just before this passage: once dawn breaks on the sixteenth of ניסן, the new grain is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we think of the עומר offering as the thing that permits the new crop. ריש לקיש's position is that the arrival of the day itself, at dawn, already permits it, even before the עומר is actually brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The eastern sky lights up, meaning dawn
Permits
The new crop of grain, forbidden until the time of the עומר

phrases.english: The illumination of the eastern horizon permits [the new crop].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a citation of ריש לקיש begun before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dawn of the sixteenth of ניסן permits the new grain, even before the עומר is brought.

steps.title: This rule was not said outright but inferred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that ריש לקיש never stated this rule directly. It was worked out from another statement of his.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of ריש לקיש was not said explicitly. Rather, it was said by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it tells us that ריש לקיש's rule comes from an inference, and it is about to show us the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of statements: ones a sage says in plain words (בְּפֵירוּשׁ), and ones we work out from something else he said (מִכְּלָלָא). Here the גמרא puts ריש לקיש's rule in the second group. That tells us the proof is coming in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, in plain words
By inference, worked out from a broader statement

phrases.english: And this [statement] of Reish Lakish
was not stated explicitly;
rather, it was stated by inference,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the rule in step 1 is known: by inference, not explicit statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש's rule is derived from another statement of his, not stated directly.

steps.title: The משנה: new-grain offerings before the עומר are invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: offerings from the new grain may not be brought before the עומר, and if they were brought, they are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: one may not bring a מנחה, ביכורים, or the מנחה that comes with an animal offering before the עומר. This is because we require offerings to be 'from the well-watered pastures of Israel.' If he brought them, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה that ריש לקיש later comments on. This is the base text for the inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the עומר, the new grain is still forbidden to the Jewish people. The גמרא adds a reason in the middle of the quote: an offering must come from what Jews are allowed to have. Since the new grain is not yet allowed, an offering made from it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the sixteenth of ניסן, which permits the new grain
The flour offering brought along with the נסכים of an animal sacrifice
From the well-watered pastures of Israel, meaning from what is permitted to Jews
Invalid

phrases.english: As we learned [in a mishna]: One may not bring
a meal offering, the first fruits, or the meal offering of an animal
phrases.notes: Read this as a list of three: a מנחה, ביכורים, and the flour that comes with an animal's נסכים.

phrases.english: prior to the omer,
since we require [offerings to be] "from the well-watered pastures of Israel,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 45:15. This reason is the גמרא's own words, added in the middle of the משנה.

phrases.english: And if he brought [them], they are unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֵין מְבִיאִין מִנְחַת בִּכּוּרִים וּמִנְחַת בְּהֵמָה קוֹדֶם לָעוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source from which ריש לקיש's view is inferred.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings from the new grain brought before the עומר are פסול.

steps.title: Before the two loaves: not allowed, but valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: after the עומר but before the שתי הלחם, one should not bring these offerings, but if he did, they are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before the two loaves he should not bring them, because the two loaves are called 'first fruits.' But if he brought them, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with the second time period, between the עומר and שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the עומר has been brought, the new grain is permitted. So bringing an offering from it is only a matter of order: the שתי הלחם are called 'first,' so they should come first. That is why the offering is כשר after the fact, unlike the case before the עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות
First fruits; here, a name given to the שתי הלחם
Valid

phrases.english: Prior to the two loaves one may not bring [them],
because [the two loaves] are called "first fruits,"
But if he brought [them], they are fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the period between the עומר and שתי הלחם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings from the new grain brought before the שתי הלחם are not allowed in the first place, but are כשר after the fact.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Before the עומר the offering is פסול, because the grain itself is still forbidden. Before the שתי הלחם it is כשר after the fact, because only the order was wrong.

steps.title: ריש לקיש limits the invalid case to the fourteenth and fifteenth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה's פסול ruling applies only on the fourteenth and fifteenth of ניסן. On the sixteenth, even before the עומר, the offering is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said in the name of ריש לקיש: They taught this only on the fourteenth and fifteenth. But on the sixteenth, if he brought it, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is ריש לקיש's statement on the משנה, which is the key to the inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש narrows the first ruling of the משנה. On the sixteenth, the day of the עומר, an offering brought before the עומר itself is still כשר. Something about the day has already changed the grain's status.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of; a phrase that limits a ruling
The sixteenth of ניסן, the day the עומר is offered

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzḥak says that Reish Lakish says:
They taught [this] only
on the fourteenth or on the fifteenth [of Nisan],
but on the sixteenth,
if he brought [it], it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר וּבַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the first ruling of the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offering from the new grain brought on the sixteenth of ניסן, even before the עומר, is כשר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's own difficulty: lacking the proper time
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש admits his ruling is hard for him: such offerings should be treated like a מחוסר זמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is difficult for me: let them be like offerings whose time has not yet come!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש raises a question against his own ruling: since the עומר was not yet brought, shouldn't these offerings count as too early?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering brought before its proper time (מחוסר זמן) is פסול. If the עומר is what permits the grain, then an offering brought before the עומר should be too early. Even so, ריש לקיש does not take back his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: This is difficult for me
Lacking time; an offering brought before its proper time, which is פסול

phrases.english: And it is difficult for me:
Let them be like [offerings] whose time has not yet arrived!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: ריש לקיש questions his own ruling from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that offerings brought on the sixteenth before the עומר are כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before the עומר the grain seems not yet permitted, so an offering from it should be פסול as a מחוסר זמן.

steps.title: So ריש לקיש holds that dawn permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes: since ריש לקיש rules the offering כשר anyway, he must hold that dawn of the sixteenth permits the new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Evidently, he holds that the light of the eastern sky permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the inference it promised in step 2. This is where ריש לקיש's rule from step 1 comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only way an offering brought before the עומר on the sixteenth could be כשר is if the grain was already permitted at that point. That means dawn itself permitted it. So the rule in step 1 is proven from ריש לקיש's ruling, even though he never said it in those words.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see
He holds, he is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש rules that offerings from the new grain brought on the sixteenth of ניסן, even before the עומר, are כשר. From this ruling the גמרא infers that he holds dawn (הֵאִיר מִזְרָח) permits the new grain.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, for ריש לקיש, the day itself permits the new grain, not only the act of bringing the עומר. This idea is what the גמרא was relying on before this passage.

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds
the illumination of the eastern [horizon] permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that despite the difficulty in step 6, ריש לקיש's ruling proves his view; this closes the derivation announced in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש holds that dawn of the sixteenth of ניסן permits the new grain, as shown by his ruling that offerings brought that day before the עומר are כשר.

steps.title: רבא: the עומר stays valid even with wrong intent
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a מנחת העומר whose handful was taken שלא לשמה is כשר, its leftovers are eaten, and no second עומר is needed. Wrong intent only works with a fit person, a fit item, and a fit place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: if the כהן took the handful from the עומר offering with the wrong intent, it is still valid. The rest of it is eaten, and we do not need another עומר to permit the new grain. This is because wrong intent only ruins an offering when it comes from a person fit for the עבודה, about an item fit for the עבודה, in a place fit for the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion about a מנחת העומר whose handful was taken with the wrong intent. רבא holds it is completely valid and does its full job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier view on the דף said this עומר is פסול, and another said it is כשר but a second עומר is still needed. רבא goes further: it is כשר and fully permits the new grain. His reason is a general rule that wrong intent only takes effect under three conditions of fitness.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake, meaning done with the intent of a different offering
Taking the handful of flour from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
The leftover part of the מנחה, which the כהנים eat
Intent of the כהן during the עבודה
Fit for the Temple service

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's three-part rule (person, item, place) is a general principle about when wrong intent can ruin a קרבן.

phrases.english: And Rava says:
An omer meal offering from which he took the handful not for its own sake –
is valid, and its remainder is eaten,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר אַחֶרֶת לְהַתִּירָהּ,
phrases.english: and it does not need another omer offering to permit it,
because intent does not take effect
except with one who is fit for the service,
and with an item that is fit for the service,
and in a place that is fit for the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁקְּמָצָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier discussion on the דף about an עומר done שלא לשמה and gives a third opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחת העומר whose handful was taken שלא לשמה is fully כשר and permits the new grain, because wrong intent needs a fit person, a fit item, and a fit place.

steps.title: רבא explains each of his three conditions
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains what each condition leaves out: a בעל מום כהן, the מנחת העומר (since it is a חידוש), and a damaged מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A person fit for the service' leaves out a כהן with a blemish. 'An item fit for the service' leaves out the עומר offering, which is not considered fit because it is a one-time novelty. 'A place fit for the service' leaves out a time when the מזבח is damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא spells out what each of his three conditions is meant to exclude. The middle one is the reason his ruling about the עומר works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished כהן cannot do the עבודה, so his intent does nothing. The עומר is an unusual offering, a חידוש, so for the rules of intent it does not count as 'fit,' and wrong intent cannot ruin it. When the מזבח is damaged the place is not fit, so wrong intent at that time also does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone with a physical blemish (here a כהן), who may not do the עבודה
To exclude, to leave out
A novelty, an unusual case that breaks the normal pattern
The מזבח became damaged

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the עומר is not a real קרבן. It is a real מנחה. It is only treated as an exception when it comes to the rules of wrong intent.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבא, wrong intent only ruins a קרבן with a fit person, a fit item, and a fit place. The עומר is an exception on 'fit item,' so it stays fully כשר.

phrases.english: 'With one who is fit for the service' –
to exclude a blemished priest,
'and with an item that is fit for the service' –
to exclude the omer offering, which is not fit,
since it is a novelty,
'and in a place that is fit for the service' –
to exclude when the altar was damaged.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִי שֶׁרָאוּי לָעֲבוֹדָה – לְאַפּוֹקֵי כֹּהֵן בַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each part of the three-part rule from Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three conditions exclude a בעל מום כהן, the מנחת העומר, and a damaged מזבח.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 'מן הבקר' excludes a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the extra words 'מן הבקר' teach that a טרפה may not be brought as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: when the פסוק says 'from the cattle' a second time, lower down, there was no need to say it. So it comes to exclude a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: which animals are forbidden on the מזבח. A ברייתא learns from a repeated phrase in the פסוק that a טרפה is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מן הבקר' already appeared in the earlier פסוק. Since the second time seems unneeded, it must teach something new, and that new teaching is that a טרפה is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury or defect; forbidden to eat
There was no need for the פסוק to say it, so it must be teaching something
Lower down, in the following פסוק

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
When it says 'of the herd' further down,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3, right after ויקרא 1:2, which already said 'from the cattle.'

phrases.english: where there is no need for the verse to say it,
rather, it comes to exclude the tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״מִן הַבָּקָר״ לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, separate from רבא's rule about intent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טרפה is excluded from being a קרבן, learned from the extra words 'מן הבקר'.

steps.title: Why not learn it from a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why we need a פסוק. A בעל מום is allowed to eat yet forbidden on the מזבח, so a טרפה, which is forbidden even to eat, should surely be forbidden on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can't we figure this out with logic? A blemished animal is allowed for a regular person to eat, yet it is forbidden for the מזבח. A טרפה is forbidden even for a regular person, so isn't it obvious that it is forbidden for the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own source. It suggests a קל וחומר would teach the rule without needing the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic: the מזבח is stricter than a regular person, since even a בעל מום that a person may eat is forbidden there. So something a regular person may not eat, a טרפה, should surely be forbidden on the מזבח. If so, the extra words seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? This opens a קל וחומר
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
An ordinary person (eating regular food)
'The One on High,' meaning the מזבח, as an offering

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical inference?
If a blemished animal, which is permitted to an ordinary person –
is forbidden for the Most High,
a tereifa, which is forbidden to an ordinary person –
isn't it logical that it is forbidden for the Most High?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the פסוק in Step 10 is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the extra words 'מן הבקר' to exclude a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from בעל מום should already forbid a טרפה, so the פסוק would be unnecessary.

steps.title: חלב and דם break the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: חלב and דם are forbidden to a regular person yet are offered on the מזבח, so 'forbidden to a person' does not mean 'forbidden on the מזבח.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Fat and blood prove otherwise: they are forbidden to a regular person, but they are allowed for the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר with a counterexample. This shows why the פסוק is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that whatever a person may not eat is surely not allowed on the מזבח. חלב and דם disprove this: people may not eat them, yet they are exactly what goes on the מזבח. Since logic fails, we need the extra words of the פסוק to exclude a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (otherwise); a counterexample that breaks a קל וחומר
Forbidden fats of an animal, which are burned on the מזבח
Blood, forbidden to eat but sprinkled on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage the קל וחומר seems to fail, so the פסוק would be needed (the ברייתא will challenge this counter-example in the next step). חלב and דם show that 'forbidden to a person' does not automatically mean 'forbidden to the מזבח.'

phrases.english: Fat and blood will prove otherwise,
as they are forbidden to an ordinary person and permitted for the Most High!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from Step 11 and so defends the need for the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from בעל מום to טרפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Its assumption that what is forbidden to a person must be forbidden to the מזבח is false, as חלב and דם show.

steps.title: Fat and blood are different because they come from a permitted animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on the חלב and דם comparison. Those come from an animal that is permitted to eat, but a טרפה is entirely forbidden, so it should not go on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about fat and blood? They come from something that is generally permitted. Can you say the same about a טרפה, which is completely forbidden? It should not be allowed for the Most High!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the last step's attack on the קל וחומר. It shows that חלב and דם are not a fair comparison to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 argued that something forbidden to a person can still go on the מזבח, like חלב and דם. Here the ברייתא answers that חלב and דם are only parts of an animal that is itself permitted to eat. A טרפה is forbidden as a whole animal, so the קל וחומר stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: From something generally permitted (the animal itself may be eaten)
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
The Most High, meaning use on the מזבח
'What about...?' A formula that points out how one case is different from another

phrases.english: What about fat and blood?
phrases.notes: He is answering the proof from Step 12, which used חלב and דם.

phrases.english: They are special, since they come from something generally permitted,
will you say the same about a tereifa, which is entirely forbidden,
and so should not be permitted for the Most High!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחֵלֶב וָדָם, שֶׁכֵּן בָּאִין מִכְּלַל הֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 12's rejection, which brings back the קל וחומר from Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the חלב and דם counter-example only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חלב and דם come from a permitted animal, while a טרפה is forbidden as a whole, so they are not comparable.

steps.title: A pinched bird proves that a fully forbidden item can still be offered
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a new counter-example: a bird killed by מליקה is fully forbidden to eat for a regular person, yet it is offered on the מזבח. So the קל וחומר fails again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Pinching will prove it: a pinched bird is completely forbidden, forbidden to an ordinary person, and yet permitted for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks the קל וחומר again with a better example, a bird קרבן killed by מליקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said a טרפה is different because it is forbidden as a whole. A pinched bird is also forbidden as a whole to a regular person, since pinching is not proper שחיטה. Yet it is the normal way to bring a bird קרבן, so 'fully forbidden to people' still does not mean 'forbidden on the מזבח'.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird קרבן by the כהן pinching the back of its neck with his fingernail
'Will prove.' Brings a case that breaks a proposed rule
An ordinary person (as opposed to the מזבח)

phrases.english: Pinching will prove it,
since it is entirely forbidden,
and it is forbidden to an ordinary person,
yet it is permitted for the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by giving a counter-example that is fully forbidden, not just partly.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the restored קל וחומר from Steps 11 and 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A pinched bird is entirely forbidden to people yet allowed on the מזבח, so being fully forbidden to eat does not decide fitness for the מזבח.

steps.title: Pinching is different because its holiness is what makes it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the מליקה proof. A pinched bird only becomes forbidden at the moment it is made holy for the מזבח, but a טרפה is forbidden on its own, not because of any holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about pinching? It is special, since its holiness is what forbids it. Only at the time it becomes holy for the מזבח, which is the pinching, does it become forbidden to a person. Before that, it was not forbidden. That is not true of a טרפה, whose holiness does not forbid it!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the מליקה proof from Step 14, which brings the קל וחומר back once more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pinched bird becomes forbidden only through the act of pinching, which is the קרבן service itself. So its being forbidden comes from its holiness, and that cannot disqualify it. A טרפה was already forbidden before any holiness, so the logic that it should be unfit for the מזבח stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Its holiness is what makes it forbidden
The altar
Which is not so (with the other case)

phrases.english: What about pinching?
It is special, since its holiness forbids it,
at the time of its holiness for the altar
it becomes forbidden to an ordinary person,
which is the moment of its pinching,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קוֹדֶם לָכֵן לֹא נֶאֶסְרָה לַהֶדְיוֹט,
phrases.english: but before that it was not forbidden to an ordinary person,
which is not so with a tereifa,
since its holiness does not forbid it!
phrases.notes: A טרפה was already forbidden because of its defect, before it was ever made holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 14's counter-example, which brings back the קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pinched bird's prohibition comes from its own holiness, while a טרפה's prohibition exists before and apart from holiness.

steps.title: The extra words 'מן הבקר' exclude a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes: if you managed to refute the reasoning, the extra words 'מן הבקר' written later in the פסוק are not needed for anything else, so they come to exclude a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you have refuted it, when the פסוק says 'from the herd' further on, and there is no need to say it, it comes to exclude a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the back-and-forth by pointing to the פסוק itself as the source that a טרפה is unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if the logic can be broken, we still have a source: the words 'מן הבקר' are extra, and extra words in a פסוק teach something new. What they teach is that a טרפה may not be brought as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: You have answered back, meaning you found a way to refute the argument
There is no need for the פסוק to say it (so the words are extra)
To exclude
'From the herd', the extra words in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא tests a קל וחומר through several rounds (חלב and דם, then מליקה), and in the end grounds the rule that a טרפה is unfit for the מזבח in the extra words 'מן הבקר'.
steps.confusionAlert: The last round (Step 15) actually supported the קל וחומר, yet this line says 'if you have refuted it.' That sounds surprising, and the גמרא itself goes on to discuss what this line means.

phrases.english: And if you have refuted it,
when it says 'from the herd' further on,
since there is no need for the verse to say it,
it comes to exclude the tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הֵשַׁבְתָּה, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״מִן הַבָּקָר״ לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the back-and-forth of Steps 11-15 by returning to the פסוק from Step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The extra words 'מן הבקר' are the source that a טרפה may not be brought as a קרבן, even though the logic was debated back and forth.

steps.title: What refutation did the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what refutation the ברייתא was hinting at when it said 'if you refuted.' It also gives a memory aid for the coming discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'if you refuted'? (Memory aid: Rekiach, Mar, Adda, Leshisheih.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what refutation of the קל וחומר the ברייתא had in mind. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא knocked down two refutations (חלב and דם, and מליקה), so the קל וחומר seemed to stand. Yet it ended with 'if you refuted,' which means there must be some refutation that works. The גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: If you refuted; if you answered back against the argument
Memory aid, a hint to help remember the order of the discussion

phrases.english: What is the 'if you refuted'?
(Memory aid: Rekiach, Mar, Adda, Leshisheih.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא's closing phrase in step 16 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which refutation makes the קל וחומר fail, so that the פסוק is needed to exclude a טרפה.

steps.title: רב: the מנחת העומר refutes the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the refutation is the מנחת העומר. It is forbidden to a regular person, yet it is offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Because one can say that the עומר meal offering proves the point. It is forbidden to a regular person, yet it is allowed for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: רב names the refutation. The מנחת העומר is something forbidden to people that still goes on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said that what is forbidden to a person should surely be forbidden on the מזבח. The עומר is made of new grain, which no one may eat before the עומר is brought, yet it is offered on the מזבח. So 'forbidden to a person' does not prove 'forbidden on the מזבח,' and a פסוק is needed to exclude a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
Will prove; shows the rule does not hold
A regular person
The Most High; the מזבח and offerings

phrases.english: Rav said:
Because it can be said:
the עומר meal offering will prove it,
for it is forbidden to a regular person,
and permitted for the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The refutation is the מנחת העומר, which is forbidden to people but offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: The עומר is special because it permits new grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב's proof. The עומר is unusual because it makes the new grain permitted, and a טרפה permits nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the עומר meal offering? It is special because it permits the new grain!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב. The עומר is a special case and can't be compared to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר has a job: bringing it makes the whole new crop permitted to eat. That special power could be why it is allowed on the מזבח even though it is forbidden to people. A טרפה has no such power, so the עומר does not break the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes permitted
New grain of this year, forbidden until the עומר is brought

phrases.english: What about the עומר meal offering?
It is special, since it permits the new grain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's proof from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב's use of the עומר as a refutation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The עומר has a special quality, permitting חדש, that a טרפה lacks.

steps.title: The עומר of the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: The answer: take the עומר brought in שביעית. No one planted that year, so there is no new crop for it to permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by pointing to the עומר brought in the שמיטה year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית planting is forbidden, so there is no new crop. That עומר permits nothing, yet it is still offered. So the special power to permit חדש is not the reason it goes on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, שמיטה, when fields are left alone

phrases.english: In the seventh year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a case where the special quality is missing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עומר is allowed on the מזבח only because it permits חדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שביעית עומר permits nothing and is still offered.

steps.title: Even in שביעית the עומר permits ספיחין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even in שביעית, the עומר permits the ספיחין, plants that grew by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the seventh year too, it permits the plants that grew by themselves that year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the שביעית answer. Even then the עומר still permits something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some grain grows on its own in שביעית without being planted. The עומר makes that grain permitted. So even the שביעית עומר keeps its special power, and the difference from a טרפה comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Plants that grew on their own, without being planted

phrases.english: The seventh year also,
since it permits the self-grown plants in the seventh year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שביעית עומר permits nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It still permits ספיחין, so it still has the special quality.

steps.title: Following רבי עקיבא, ספיחין are forbidden anyway
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that ספיחין are forbidden in שביעית. So the עומר permits nothing that year.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי עקיבא, who says that self-grown plants are forbidden in the seventh year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רב's proof by relying on רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ספיחין are forbidden anyway, the עומר of שביעית can't permit them. So that עומר permits nothing, yet it is offered. That shows 'forbidden to a person' does not mean 'forbidden on the מזבח.'

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden

phrases.english: In accordance with רבי עקיבא,
who says: self-grown plants are forbidden in the seventh year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the proof to a specific תנא's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי עקיבא ספיחין are forbidden anyway, so the עומר permits nothing.

steps.title: Even for רבי עקיבא, the עומר permits new grain outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אבא challenges רב אשי: even for רבי עקיבא, the שביעית עומר permits new grain grown outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אבא said to רב אשי: Even according to רבי עקיבא, let us refute: what about the עומר meal offering? It permits new grain outside the Land!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge comes against the רבי עקיבא answer. Even in שביעית, the עומר still permits something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיטה applies only in ארץ ישראל, so outside the Land people plant as usual. The עומר makes that new grain permitted too. So even in שביעית and even for רבי עקיבא, the עומר keeps its special power, and the refutation fails again.

keyTerms.meaning: To refute; to knock down an argument
Outside ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not arguing with רבי עקיבא about ספיחין. He agrees ספיחין are forbidden, but points out the עומר still permits something else.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Abba said to Rav Ashi:
Even according to Rabbi Akiva, let us refute:
What about the עומר meal offering?
It is special, since it permits new grain outside the Land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, for רבי עקיבא, the שביעית עומר permits nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It still permits חדש grown outside ארץ ישראל, so it keeps the special quality that sets it apart from a טרפה.

steps.title: Even without outside grain, the עומר permits itself
steps.stepSummary: Even for the view that חדש outside ארץ ישראל is only rabbinic, the עומר is still unusual: it permits the prohibition inside itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to the one who says that new grain outside ארץ ישראל is not forbidden by Torah law, the עומר is still different, because it comes to permit a prohibition that is inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר אבא keeps pushing back on the answer from Step 22. Even if the outside-the-Land grain does not count, the שביעית עומר still permits something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said the שביעית עומר permits new grain grown outside ארץ ישראל. Someone could answer that this is only rabbinic. So רב אחא בר אבא gives a second reason the עומר is unusual: once its handful is burned, the rest of the עומר flour becomes permitted to the כהנים. Either way, the עומר still permits something, and a טרפה permits nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: New grain, forbidden to eat until the עומר is brought
Outside ארץ ישראל
From the Torah (not just rabbinic)
A prohibition on the offering's own contents

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says
new grain outside the Land is not forbidden by Torah law,
[the עומר is different] since it comes to permit a prohibition that is inside it.
phrases.notes: The 'prohibition inside it' is the rest of the עומר flour. Once the handful is burned on the מזבח, the כהנים may eat the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger reason to the challenge in Step 23, so the challenge still works even if the outside grain does not count.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 22 that the שביעית עומר (according to רבי עקיבא) permits nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with no crop to permit, the עומר still permits its own leftover flour to the כהנים, so it stays different from a טרפה.

steps.title: Then a טרפה could permit itself too
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי objects: by that reasoning, a טרפה offered on the מזבח would also permit its own meat to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא from דיפתי said to רבינא: If so, a טרפה should also be offered, and it would permit the prohibition that is inside it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי attacks the reason given in Step 24. He says it is not a real difference between the עומר and a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טרפה were allowed on the מזבח, offering it would also make its meat permitted to the כהנים. So 'permitting what is inside it' is not unique to the עומר. That means it cannot be used to say the עומר is special.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is right)
Be offered on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina:
If so,
a טרפה too should be offered
and permit the prohibition that is inside it!
phrases.notes: Once offered, the טרפה's meat would become permitted for the כהנים to eat, the same as the עומר's leftover flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the reason given in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the עומר is special because it permits what is inside it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same thing would happen with a טרפה if it were offered. So this is not a real difference between the עומר and a טרפה, and it proves nothing.

steps.title: The real difference: the עומר is commanded this way
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי gives a better way to reject רב's proof: the עומר's מצוה is to be brought from the forbidden new grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, refute it this way: what is special about the עומר meal offering? Its מצוה is to be brought this way.
steps.whatsHappening: After knocking down the reason from Step 24, רב אחא מדיפתי gives a new and stronger reason why the עומר cannot be compared to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah commands that the עומר be brought from the new grain, which is still forbidden at that point. Nothing commands us to offer a טרפה. So the fact that the עומר is forbidden to ordinary people but offered on the מזבח tells us nothing about a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Refute it this way
The barley meal offering brought on the 16th of ניסן
This is exactly how its מצוה is done

steps.whatToRemember: The final rejection of the עומר proof: the עומר is commanded to be brought from forbidden new grain, but a טרפה has no such מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, refute it like this:
What is special about the עומר meal offering?
That its מצוה is this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reason knocked down in Step 25 with a better one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב's proof from the עומר completely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The עומר is offered because the Torah commands it to come from forbidden grain. That special מצוה does not apply to a טרפה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש brings proof from the incense maker
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says a פסוק is needed for טרפה because the קטורת case could break the קל וחומר: it is forbidden to ordinary people but permitted for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: a פסוק is needed because one could say, 'the one who prepares the קטורת proves it,' since it is forbidden for an ordinary person and permitted for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different case that could break the קל וחומר about טרפה. This explains why the Torah needed a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said: if something forbidden to ordinary people (a טרפה) is involved, surely it is forbidden on the מזבח. ריש לקיש points to the קטורת. People may not make it for themselves, yet it is made for the בית המקדש. So 'forbidden to ordinary people' does not always mean 'forbidden for the מזבח.'

keyTerms.meaning: The person who mixes the incense
Will prove (this case breaks the logic)
An ordinary person, for private use
The Most High, use for the מקדש or מזבח

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
because one can say
the one who prepares the incense proves it,
for it is forbidden to an ordinary person and permitted for the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different case from the עומר to explain why a פסוק is needed for טרפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת shows that something forbidden to ordinary people can still be permitted for the מזבח, so the קל וחומר about טרפה could be broken.

steps.title: But the preparer is a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions ריש לקיש's wording: a preparer is a person, so how can he be 'forbidden'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the one who prepares is a person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the exact words ריש לקיש used. It is not attacking his idea yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'the preparer is forbidden to an ordinary person' makes no sense. A person is not something that is forbidden or permitted. The wording needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: A person (a man)

phrases.english: The one who prepares is a person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word מְפַטֵּם in ריש לקיש's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule 'forbidden to ordinary people, permitted for the Most High' describes an act or an object, not a person.

steps.title: He meant the preparing of the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the act of preparing the קטורת is what proves the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the preparing of the קטורת proves it, since it is forbidden for an ordinary person and permitted for the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes ריש לקיש's words so they make sense, and his idea stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing מְפַטֵּם (preparer) to פִּטּוּם (preparing) points to the act itself. Mixing the קטורת recipe is forbidden for private use but required for the מקדש. Now the case can be tested as a real challenge to the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The act of mixing the incense

phrases.english: Rather, the preparing of the incense proves it,
for it is forbidden to an ordinary person and permitted for the Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in Step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש was talking about the person who prepares the incense.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the act of preparing it.

steps.title: The incense is also commanded this way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects ריש לקיש's proof: preparing the קטורת is a מצוה for the מקדש, unlike offering a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about preparing the קטורת? That its מצוה is this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down ריש לקיש's case with the same answer it used for the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah commands us to mix the קטורת for the מקדש, so of course it is permitted there. There is no מצוה to offer a טרפה. So the קטורת cannot break the קל וחומר either.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about...? (pointing out a difference to reject a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: Both the עומר and the קטורת fail as proofs for the same reason: each is commanded to be done that way, and a טרפה is not.

phrases.english: What is special about preparing the incense?
That its מצוה is this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְפִטּוּם הַקְּטֹרֶת, שֶׁכֵּן מִצְוָתוֹ בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the corrected version of ריש לקיש's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects ריש לקיש's proof from the קטורת completely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The קטורת is prepared because the Torah commands it, and a טרפה has no such מצוה.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא: שבת shows the קל וחומר can fail
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא says a פסוק is needed for טרפה because שבת could break the קל וחומר. Work on שבת is forbidden to ordinary people but permitted for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא said: we need a פסוק because someone could say, 'Look at שבת! Work is forbidden for ordinary people, but it is permitted for the service of the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives his own answer to the same question ריש לקיש was answering. He explains why a פסוק is needed to disqualify a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that anything forbidden to a person is surely forbidden for the מזבח. מר בריה דרבינא points to שבת as a counter-example. מלאכה is forbidden to people, yet the עבודה in the מקדש is done on שבת. So the logic alone is not enough, and a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove: a case that shows a logical argument does not always work
An ordinary person, as opposed to the holy service
Literally 'the Most High': the מזבח and the עבודה in the מקדש
Because one could say: introduces a possible objection to a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, said:
Because it can be said:
Shabbat proves it,
for it is forbidden to an ordinary person
and permitted for the Most High.
phrases.notes: This is about the work of bringing קרבנות in the מקדש, which is done even on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא אָמַר, מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ריש לקיש's קטורת example was just rejected, so a different אמורא offers a new counter-example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת is forbidden to a הדיוט but permitted for גבוה, so it can break the קל וחומר. Therefore a פסוק is needed for טרפה.

steps.title: שבת is weaker because it is permitted for מילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the שבת example. שבת is already pushed aside for an ordinary person in the case of מילה, so it cannot teach us about טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What can you learn from שבת? שבת is special, because even for an ordinary person its prohibition was lifted for מילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects מר בריה דרבינא's proof. It says שבת is a weaker איסור, so it cannot be compared to טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A counter-example only works if it is as strong as the case it is compared to. שבת already gives way for an ordinary person when doing a ברית מילה. So it is no surprise that it also gives way for the מזבח. טרפה has no such exception, so שבת proves nothing about it.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The standard way to point out what makes one case different from another
Was permitted out of its general rule: the איסור has an exception
ברית מילה, which is done on its proper day even on שבת

phrases.english: What about Shabbat?
For it was permitted from its general prohibition
for an ordinary person in the case of circumcision!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the שבת counter-example given in step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from שבת only. Another answer to why a פסוק is needed comes from רב אדא בר אבא in step 35.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שבת is already permitted for an ordinary person in the case of מילה, so it is a weaker איסור than טרפה.

steps.title: But circumcision is a מצוה, not a personal need
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions its own rejection. מילה is not an ordinary person's private need. It is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is מילה just a need of an ordinary person? מילה is a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just gave. It says the מילה example does not fit the description 'permitted for an ordinary person.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection said שבת was lifted 'for a הדיוט.' But doing a ברית on שבת is allowed only because it is a מצוה, not for personal comfort. So it is not really a case of שבת giving way to ordinary needs, and the rejection as worded does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? Introduces a surprised challenge
The need of an ordinary person: a private, personal need
A commandment; something done because the תורה commands it

phrases.english: Is that to say circumcision is an ordinary person's need?
Circumcision is a מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of the rejection in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection in step 32, which said שבת was permitted 'for an ordinary person' through מילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מילה is permitted on שבת because it is a מצוה, not because of a personal need. So it does not show that שבת is a weak איסור for ordinary people.

steps.title: Better rejection: bringing offerings on שבת is itself a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects מר בריה דרבינא in a new way. On שבת, bringing קרבנות is a מצוה, but there is no מצוה to bring a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here is the real difference: What can you learn from שבת? On שבת, the מצוה is to do exactly this, to bring קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the מילה argument. It gives a better reason why שבת cannot break the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה commands that קרבנות be brought on שבת, so the עבודה is permitted because it is a מצוה. Nobody is commanded to offer a טרפה. So שבת is not a fair comparison, and the proof falls. This matches how the גמרא rejected the עומר and the קטורת in steps 26 and 30.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous idea and replaces it with a better one
Its מצוה is in this way: the act itself is what the תורה commands

steps.whatToRemember: A case that is permitted for the מזבח because it is a מצוה (עומר, קטורת, שבת) cannot be used to permit a טרפה, because there is no מצוה to bring a טרפה.

phrases.english: Rather, what about Shabbat?
For its מצוה is in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מָה לְשַׁבָּת שֶׁכֵּן מִצְוָתָהּ בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejection from step 32, which step 33 knocked down, with a stronger rejection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The שבת proof of מר בריה דרבינא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עבודה on שבת is itself a מצוה, while there is no מצוה to offer a טרפה, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אבא: כלאים show the קל וחומר can fail
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אבא gives a new reason why a פסוק is needed. כלאים are forbidden to ordinary people but permitted for the מזבח's service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אבא said: we need a פסוק because someone could say, 'Look at כלאים! They are forbidden to ordinary people but permitted for the service of the מקדש.'
steps.whatsHappening: After the שבת example was rejected, another אמורא suggests a new counter-example, כלאים. He wants to explain why a פסוק is needed for טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary person may not wear wool and linen mixed together. Yet the כהן's garments used in the עבודה contained such a mixture. This seems to show that something forbidden to people can still be allowed for גבוה. So the קל וחומר would not be enough, and a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures; here, cloth of wool and linen together (שעטנז)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Abba said:
Because it can be said,
diverse kinds proves it,
for they are forbidden to an ordinary person
and permitted for the Most High.
phrases.notes: This is about the כהן's garments, like the belt, which were made with wool and linen mixed together.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שבת example was rejected in step 34, a new אמורא offers a new counter-example.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלאים are forbidden to a הדיוט but permitted for גבוה, so they can break the קל וחומר. Therefore a פסוק is needed for טרפה.

steps.title: כלאים is already allowed for an ordinary person with ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אדא בר אבא's proof. כלאים is already allowed even for an ordinary person in the case of ציצית, so it cannot teach us anything about טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about כלאים? Its general prohibition was already lifted for an ordinary person, with ציצית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אדא בר אבא. It says כלאים is not a strong example, because even an ordinary person is sometimes allowed to wear כלאים, with ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אבא wanted to show that some things forbidden to ordinary people are still allowed for the מזבח. That would break the קל וחומר and prove we need a פסוק for טרפה. But if כלאים is already loosened for ordinary people too, it is a weaker prohibition, and it cannot show that the מזבח is treated more leniently than a person.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden mixtures; here, wool and linen worn together (שעטנז)
they were permitted out of their general prohibition
an ordinary person, as opposed to the מזבח or holy service
fringes on a four-cornered garment

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same move the גמרא made with שבת and מילה in step 32. Only the example has changed, from שבת to כלאים, and from מילה to ציצית.

phrases.english: What is special about כלאים?
That they were permitted out of their general rule
for an ordinary person, with ציצית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אדא בר אבא's כלאים example from step 35.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the כלאים example. The need for a פסוק is not yet settled.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כלאים is already permitted for ordinary people with ציצית, so it does not show special leniency for the מזבח.

steps.title: ציצית is a מצוה, not a private need
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions its own rejection. ציצית is not an ordinary person's personal need. It is a מצוה. Then the גמרא says 'אלא' to set up a new rejection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is ציצית an ordinary person's private need? It is a מצוה! Rather...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges what it just said. ציצית is a מצוה, so it is not a case of an ordinary person's private needs. The final word 'אלא' tells us the גמרא is about to reject רב אדא בר אבא in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection in step 36 needed כלאים to be allowed for a plain, personal reason. But ציצית is a מצוה, just like מילה in step 33, so it does not count. The rejection falls apart, and the גמרא gets ready to give a better one.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (a questioning word that expects a 'no')
an ordinary person's private need
a commandment, a religious duty
rather; it introduces a new approach

steps.whatToRemember: Allowing something for a מצוה, like מילה or ציצית, is not the same as allowing it for an ordinary person's private needs.

phrases.english: Is ציצית an ordinary person's private need?
It is a מצוה!
Rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 36, the same way step 33 challenged step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection in step 36, which used ציצית to weaken כלאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ציצית is a מצוה, not a private need of an ordinary person. So it does not show that כלאים was loosened for ordinary people.
